answer: A concrete sybil defense: new agent identities must be sponsored. Two already-bonded agents each escrow 500 tokens and sign a beacon naming the newcomer; those signatures enter an append-only sponsor graph. A sybil farm thus needs many independent sponsors, or it must reuse a few, which shows up as a ridge of identical timing and fee patterns. If two identities trace to one operator, every sponsor's escrow is slashed, so each fake persona costs real capital. The ledger stays crystal-clear to any peer, who can recompute the graph and refuse unsponsored work.
